criteria.evidence: Umbrella over ticket 19's permissioned-read, required-identifier, query-key, pagination, runtime-parsing, cancellation, invalidation and optimistic-update criteria. Cancellation is genuinely closed (check:query-signal, 1057 queryFn blocks / 428 files, positional signal-slot resolution, empty ALLOWLIST at scripts/check-query-signal.mjs:48) and optimistic updates are closed (C098). Six of the eight sub-areas are not.
criteria.blocker: C095, C096, C097, C099, C100, C101 and C137 are all OPEN below. Closing C007 requires closing those.
criteria.clauses_failing: required-identifier (C096), query-key (C095), pagination (C099), runtime parsing (C101), invalidation (C097)

criteria.evidence: MOST clauses hold and I verified them independently, not from the prior report: (a) one hierarchical factory per domain - lib/query-keys/ has 19 domain modules + lib/query-keys.ts (3436 lines); `check:query-scope` exit 0 over 5411 files bans inline `queryKey: [` literals, hardcoded "streamlineos" prefixes and unsanctioned QueryClient/queryKeyHashFn; I grepped every `const *Keys = {` outside the registry (30 files in hooks/api/accounting/** and hooks/api/hr/**) and ALL of them compose `queryKeys.*`, so none is a competing factory. (b) prefix/hierarchy property - lib/query-keys/key-factory-contract.test.ts PASSES: >200 factories parsed, >150 with an optional tail, every short call a partialMatchKey prefix of the long one, no literal `undefined` segment, >50 partial call sites app-wide. (c) organization + subject + scope - not in any key literal; supplied globally by authenticatedScope(orgId,userId) at lib/query-scope.ts:28-33, installed as queryKeyHashFn in components/providers/query-provider.tsx:50 with a key={scope} remount, and mirrored server-side in lib/prefetch/server-query-client.ts; lib/query-scope-isolation.test.tsx PASSES. (d) filters/sort on the paged surface - I ran my own TypeScript AST pass over all 34 useInfiniteQuery call sites comparing every identifier reachable from queryFn against the queryKey text; every residual is a type name or a module-level constant, hand-confirmed on the three that looked real (hooks/api/hr/engagement.ts:239 limit="30" literal, hooks/api/hr/succession.ts:33 limit="30" literal, hooks/api/org-hierarchy.ts:72 limit=HIERARCHY_PARENT_PAGE_SIZE and status="ACTIVE" literals). 0 filter/sort dimensions outside a key across the infinite-query surface.
criteria.blocker: One named factory omits a dimension its hook actually sends: hooks/api/accounting/banking.ts:392-403 - `useReconciliationRules(bankAccountId, params: ListRulesParams = {})` where `ListRulesParams = { cursor?: string; limit?: number }` sends `toQuery(params)` to GET /finance/reconciliation/{id}/rules but keys only `bankingKeys.rules(bankAccountId)`. The cursor and limit dimensions are outside the key, so two different cursors share one cache entry. Accounting is IN the 10/10 release scope (the permission-binding gate excludes only CRM and Inventory). Latent today - the sole caller, features/accounting/banking/components/reconciliation-rules-sheet.tsx:88, passes no params - but the factory does not carry the dimension the criterion requires. TO CLOSE: add params to bankingKeys.rules(bankAccountId, params). SECONDARY GAP: key-factory-contract.test.ts parses ONLY lib/query-keys/*.ts (`readdirSync(KEY_DIR)`), so the ~30 composed local factories in hooks/api/** are outside the prefix/undefined-poisoning oracle. LATENT, no live instance: lib/query-scope.ts:38 `scopedQueryKeyHashFn` is a bare `JSON.stringify([scope, queryKey])` with no replacer, so it does NOT sort plain-object keys the way TanStack's own hashKey does - I proved the divergence in node against the installed @tanstack/react-query (`{limit:20,cursor:'abc'}` vs `{cursor:'abc',limit:20}`: hashKey equal=true, app fn equal=false). An AST sweep of every `queryKeys.*` call taking an object literal found 0 factories called at two different property orders, so nothing diverges today; the guarantee is order-of-insertion, not structural.
criteria.clauses_failing: cursor dimension (and limit) absent from bankingKeys.rules

criteria.evidence: CLAUSE 1 (effective access) substantially holds: `check:permission-binding` exit 0 - 567 backend controllers / 3646 routes indexed with 0 handlers unresolved, 439 frontend files, 1708 WRAPPER + 689 ENABLED gate sites, 2387 bindings checked, 0 unaccounted; the 13 permissioned reads whose `enabled` consults no permission are all in UNGATED_HELD_BACK (scripts/check-permission-route-binding.mjs:218) and all in CRM (11) or Inventory (2), both out of the 10/10 release; the 4 deliberate divergences are documented and 2 of them (payroll CSV export) are correct against an in-handler `assertExport()` raise the decorator scanner cannot see. hooks/api/gated-query.ts:43 composes rather than replaces: `enabled: access.allowed && (options.enabled ?? true)`. hooks/api/gated-read-suppression.test.tsx PASSES with an explicit BITE PROOF (an ungated useQuery of the same route DOES send while denied).
criteria.blocker: CLAUSE 2 (required identifiers; disabled queries must not send malformed requests) FAILS, with a live in-scope instance. hooks/api/hr/helpdesk.ts:142-148 - `useHelpdeskTicket(ticketId: number)` calls useGatedQuery("hr:helpdesk:view", {...}) with NO `enabled` property at all, so its effective enabled is `access.allowed && true`. Its only consumer, features/hr/helpdesk/ticket-detail-sheet.tsx:59, calls it as `useHelpdeskTicket(ticketId ?? 0)` where `ticketId: number | null`, and the sheet is mounted UNCONDITIONALLY by features/hr/helpdesk/queue-tab.tsx:252 and features/hr/helpdesk/my-tickets-tab.tsx:133 with `ticketId={selectedTicketId}` initialised to null. Result: every mount of the HR helpdesk queue or my-tickets tab fires `GET /hr/helpdesk/0` for any holder of hr:helpdesk:view - a malformed request from a query that was never disabled. HR is in the 10/10 scope. TO CLOSE: add `enabled: ticketId > 0` at hooks/api/hr/helpdesk.ts:143. WIDER: my TypeScript AST sweep of 1053 read call sites found 317 that interpolate an identifier into the request path, of which 37 never mention that identifier in ANY `enabled` in scope and 16 have no `enabled` in scope at all (ai-summaries.ts:11 dead, crm/automations.ts:154, crm/campaigns.ts:70+82, hr/helpdesk.ts:143, sign/public.ts:46 public-token, surveys/analytics.ts:69+77+85, surveys/assessment.ts:34+43, surveys/automations.ts:40, surveys/collectors.ts:53, surveys/live-session.ts:59+67, surveys/participants.ts:54). NO gate checks this clause: check:gated-reads scans only hooks/api/** and only for a permission marker, and check:permission-binding classifies permission keys, not identifier guards.
criteria.clauses_failing: required identifiers / disabled queries must not send malformed requests

criteria.evidence: CLAUSE 2 (roll back optimistic state safely on failure) HOLDS and I re-derived it rather than trusting the prior report. My TypeScript AST pass over hooks/ app/ features/ components/ lib/ found 1563 useMutation + useAuthorizedMutation call sites; 49 carry onMutate; of those, every site that patches a cache (setQueryData/setQueriesData) has an onError - 'onMutate+patch WITHOUT onError (no rollback): 0'. Exactly one patching site has no literal cancelQueries, hooks/api/notifications-inbox.ts:174, and I read its path: it calls beginInboxPatch(queryClient), which awaits cancelQueries on both the list and the unread-count key at hooks/api/notifications-inbox-optimistic.ts:45-46.
criteria.blocker: CLAUSE 1 ('invalidate or update EVERY affected list/detail/count/dashboard key') is UNVERIFIED - there is no oracle for it anywhere in the repo. `grep -l invalidat scripts/*.mjs` returns only check-command-catalog.mjs, check-prd-traceability-pins.mjs and check-permission-route-binding.mjs, none of which checks invalidation coverage (check:command-catalog classifies mutation hooks against permission keys). The entire evidence base is 6 spot-test files - hooks/api/dashboard-invalidation.test.ts, hooks/api/build/mutation-invalidation.test.ts, hooks/api/hr/leave-decision-invalidation.test.tsx, hooks/api/mail-send-invalidation.test.tsx, hooks/api/users-invitation-directory-invalidation.test.tsx, hooks/api/accounting/__tests__/report-invalidation.test.ts - against 1563 mutation call sites, and each asserts one hook. My AST pass also found 237 of the 1563 sites whose call expression contains no invalidateQueries/setQueryData/setQueriesData/removeQueries/resetQueries/refetchQueries text at all (a coarse measure: some invalidate through a helper such as invalidateInbox(), which I confirmed for the notifications cluster). TO CLOSE: a gate that maps each mutation's route to the read keys that route's rows feed, and fails on an affected key no mutation touches - equivalent to what the backend already has in check:cache-invalidation.
criteria.clauses_failing: invalidate or update every affected list/detail/count/dashboard key

criteria.evidence: Measured, not asserted. My TypeScript AST pass over hooks/ app/ features/ components/ lib/ (non-test) counts 1563 useMutation + useAuthorizedMutation call sites, of which only 49 use onMutate at all and 35 of those patch a cache. Every one of the 35 has an onError rollback (scan output: 'onMutate+patch WITHOUT onError (no rollback): 0 []') and every one cancels in-flight queries before patching - 34 with a literal cancelQueries inside the mutation object, and the 35th, hooks/api/notifications-inbox.ts:174, through `await beginInboxPatch(queryClient)` which awaits cancelQueries on both affected keys at hooks/api/notifications-inbox-optimistic.ts:45-46. The remaining ~1514 sites take the criterion's other branch: they await the backend result and invalidate in onSuccess/onSettled (spot-verified at hooks/api/build/custom-states.ts:61-72, which invalidates both the list and the detail key on success). The optimistic sites that exist document their concurrency semantics in-file (notifications-inbox-optimistic.ts counts distinct ids rather than occurrences, because one notification appears in the flat list and in every InfiniteData page cached under a different filter). jest over the notification/inbox suites: 17 suites / 92 tests, all pass.

CLAUSE 2 ('changing filter/sort resets pagination correctly') HOLDS, structurally and behaviourally. Structurally: my AST pass over all 34 useInfiniteQuery call sites found 0 filter or sort dimensions outside the queryKey (every residual identifier is a type name or a module-level page-size/status constant; hand-confirmed on hooks/api/hr/engagement.ts:239, hooks/api/hr/succession.ts:33 and hooks/api/org-hierarchy.ts:72), so a filter change is a different key, hence a different infinite query, hence a restart at initialPageParam. Behaviourally: hooks/api/cursor-pagination-contract.test.tsx PASSES with 'gives an unread-only read its own key and its own first page' and 'keys the two filters apart so neither can read the other's pages'. I also grepped for offset-style continuations (`allPages`, `pages.length`, `pageParam + 1`) inside getNextPageParam across the repo: zero - every infinite query is cursor-based.
criteria.blocker: CLAUSE 1 ('does not duplicate/skip records') is verified for exactly ONE of the 31 files that mount an infinite query. hooks/api/cursor-pagination-contract.test.tsx is notifications-only and is the only test in the repo that asserts record-level integrity ('accumulates every id exactly once across pages', 'continues from the lowest id on the page, not the last element', 'stops when the page is short'). The two other cursor tests assert only that the cursor parameter round-trips into the request, not that rows are neither duplicated nor skipped: hooks/api/module-access/module-access-cursor-pagination.test.tsx ('asks for members without a page number and walks forward on nextCursor') and hooks/api/timesheets-core/timesheets-cursor-pagination.test.tsx ('page 1 sends no cursor param' / 'page 2 sends nextCursor from page 1'). features/__tests__/cursor-page-size-bounds.test.ts is a DataTable window invariant, not a record-integrity check. No gate covers this at all. The 28 uncovered families include blog, build/all-work, build/projects, build/ticket-queries, chat (5 files), crm (3), hr/employees, hr/engagement, hr/leaves, hr/succession, inbox, kb (3), mail, org-hierarchy and timesheets/payroll. TO CLOSE: a shared page-walk assertion (accumulate ids across >=3 pages, assert set size == sum of page lengths and that a short page terminates) applied per infinite-query family, plus a DB-level walk under concurrent insert for the keyset routes. Related: the C095 blocker (hooks/api/accounting/banking.ts:392-403 keys no cursor) is a paged read that would serve page 2 from page 1's cache the moment a caller supplies one.
criteria.clauses_failing: cursor pagination does not duplicate/skip records

criteria.evidence: The DATA LAYER makes all eight states distinguishable and that is proved: hooks/api/read-state-contract.test.tsx PASSES with a describe block per state - loading, background refresh (incl. 'does not take the route down when the refresh itself fails'), empty, permission denied (incl. 'is distinguishable from empty, which the query flags alone cannot do'), access not yet known, revoked access ('stops the read and flips to denied when the access snapshot is withdrawn'), offline ('pauses rather than failing' + resumes), full error (incl. ApiContractError) and partial error. Supporting: lib/query-error-policy.ts readErrorReachesBoundary routes a data-less failure to the route boundary while excluding a held-data background refresh, ABORTED, 401 and suspended-membership 403; check:empty-states exit 0 over 3878 files; 196 route error.tsx boundaries; screen-level tests exist for offline and permission-denied on inbox (features/inbox/inbox-offline.test.tsx, features/inbox/inbox-permission-denied.test.tsx), notifications and mail revocation.
criteria.blocker: permission-denied and revoked-access are NOT RENDERED anywhere in release scope. useGatedQuery returns Gated<...> carrying the refusal precisely because 'a read gated shut by a missing permission looks exactly like a read that finished and found nothing' (hooks/api/gated-query.ts:16-25). I measured consumption of that field with a TypeScript AST pass: 277 gated hooks are defined; they are consumed at 407 call sites in app/, features/ and components/; 364 of those 407 sites destructure no `access` at all; and every single one of the 43 sites that DOES read it is under CRM (23 in app/(authenticated)/crm/**, 20 in features/crm/**) - `node scan | grep CONSUMES-ACCESS | grep -vi crm` returns nothing. CRM is out of the 10/10 release. So in every in-scope module a panel whose own read is gated shut renders as an empty panel, not a refusal. check:gated-reads says this about itself in its own output: 'This gate certifies request suppression, NOT that a screen renders the refusal. The unread gates are an app/** and features/** change - ticket 30, not this scanner.' Nothing renders revoked-access outside the same CRM surface either. TO CLOSE: consume the Gated access field (or a shared DeniedState component) at the in-scope panel sites, and add a gate that fails when a useGatedQuery result is destructured without `access`.

criteria.evidence: The response half is unarbitrated, and the gate that is green says so itself. `npm run check:response-contracts` exits 0 but prints: 'Seam calls scanned: 2666 / Carrying a contract: 86 (3.2%) / Unparsed: 2580 (baseline 2594) / Distinct routes: 1964, of which 74 are parsed somewhere' and then 'NOTE: 97.8% of the seam is still an unchecked cast. This gate freezes that debt; it does not retire it.' Its own header (scripts/check-response-contracts.mjs:23-27) explains why it is a ratchet and not a requirement: 'contracts/openapi.json carries 1 response schema across 3,613 operations - measured, not assumed - so a contract cannot be generated.' I re-measured that independently against the vendored spec at head: 3648 operations, of which 26 carry a 2xx response schema (0.7%). apiClient.get<T>(...) is a cast; nothing in the type system ever sees the wire, so a backend that renames or stops sending a field is accepted silently on 2580 of 2666 call sites.
criteria.blocker: 96.8% of the fetch seam has no runtime contract. A backend contract change is silently accepted on 2580 call sites, and the gate's exit 0 only certifies that the count has not risen above the recorded baseline of 2594. TO CLOSE: derive per-route response contracts from the backend's Drizzle columns and service projections (the gate warns a contract copied from the frontend's own type encodes the drift instead of catching it), or emit real 2xx response schemas into contracts/openapi.json so contracts can be generated. Also note two unmeasured seams the gate cannot see: portalApiClient (lib/portal-api-client.ts, `body.data as T`), which check:response-contracts misses because it keys on the identifier `apiClient`; and 18 unresolvable route sites in 15 files that the gate counts but cannot classify.
criteria.clauses_failing: runtime parsing cannot silently accept a backend contract change

criteria.evidence: Three of the eight dimensions are genuinely closed repo-wide. CANCELLATION: check:query-signal exit 0 over 1057 queryFn blocks in 428 files, and it is a real rule - it parses the whole queryFn body and resolves every argument BY POSITION against a SIGNAL_SLOT map (get/post/put/patch/delete = index 2, download/upload = null), so `apiClient.get(url, signal)` is reported as a signal in a non-signal slot; its ALLOWLIST is empty. RETRY: components/providers/query-provider.tsx:48 uses shouldRetryQuery (one retry max, never on a 4xx except 408/429, never on a contract violation) and mutations retry: 0. HYDRATION: 5 prefetch factories under lib/prefetch/, lib/prefetch/hydration-contract.test.ts and lib/prefetch/cache-across-navigation.test.tsx PASS, and check:query-scope rule 3 fails any dehydrate() in lib/prefetch/ that does not go through createServerQueryClient (which recomputes the same authenticatedScope hash server-side, the exact bug lib/query-scope.ts:8-16 documents). OPTIMISTIC CONCURRENCY: closed, see C098.
criteria.blocker: The criterion says 'across every module above', and four dimensions do not hold across every module. PARSING: 86 of 2666 seam calls (C101). INVALIDATION: no oracle at all, 6 spot tests against 1563 mutation sites (C097). PAGINATION: record-integrity proved for 1 of 31 infinite-query families (C099). KEY FACTORIES: hooks/api/accounting/banking.ts:392-403 omits its cursor dimension, and the key-factory contract test's corpus is lib/query-keys/*.ts only, excluding ~30 composed local factories in hooks/api/** (C095). RETRY also diverges by module: features/portal/components/portal-providers.tsx:14 builds its own QueryClient with a bare `retry: 1` and no shouldRetryQuery, so the portal retries 403s and 404s - and that file is on check:query-scope's SANCTIONED_QUERY_CLIENT allowlist (scripts/check-query-scope.mjs:12-16), so the gate cannot see it.
criteria.clauses_failing: parsing, invalidation, pagination, key factories (one site), retry (portal module)

prior_report_assessment: reports/19-audit.md was written at 886c19f2b on release/code-10-10-v2, which `git merge-base --is-ancestor` shows is NOT an ancestor of main. Every per-criterion conclusion in it that I could re-test independently reproduces at main, so nothing in it is REFUTED. Two things changed for the better between that head and main: the 5 jest failures it recorded in the query/prefetch/contract slice are gone (27 suites / 273 tests pass at head), and its 'check:gated-reads reports 1 file reading the gate, my grep finds 10, the gate under-reports by 9' finding is now 43 consumer sites by my AST pass - but its sharper conclusion, that every one of them is in CRM and no in-scope surface renders the refusal, reproduces exactly at head.
